offering_description.value: ADMA makes plasma-derived immune globulin medicines for hospitals and specialty infusion providers. It collects donor plasma at company-operated centers, uses it to manufacture medicines, and sells source plasma to other manufacturers.

primary_products.value: Intravenous immune globulin for primary immunodeficiency; hepatitis B immune globulin; source plasma

customer_segment.value: B2B: Specialty pharmaceutical distributors, hospitals, specialty infusion providers and plasma fractionators

end_markets.value: Immunodeficiency care; hepatitis B prevention; plasma-derived pharmaceutical manufacturing

revenue_model.value: product sales: Finished immune globulin medicines and source plasma for pharmaceutical manufacturing

value_chain_position.value: OEM / manufacturer: Processes donor plasma into immune globulin medicines sold to specialty distributors and healthcare providers; raw materials: Collects source plasma from donors for internal manufacturing and sales to other plasma fractionators; asset operator: Operates plasma donation centers that supply its manufacturing plant and external plasma buyers
value_chain_position.category: OEM / manufacturer; raw materials; asset operator

geography_served.value: US national: Nationwide U.S. pharmaceutical sales and U.S. plasma collection and manufacturing

specialization.value: related lines: Intravenous immune globulin, hepatitis B immune globulin and source plasma collection

distribution_channels.value: distributors / dealers: Specialty pharmaceutical distributors serving hospitals and infusion providers; direct sales: Source plasma supply agreements with pharmaceutical manufacturers

regulatory_exposure.value: high: FDA licensing and oversight of plasma collection, biologics manufacturing and finished immune globulin products

notes: Whether ADMA currently sells source plasma outside the United States is uncertain.
